items.item_text: Certification with one of the following agencies: American Association of Medical Assistants (AMA), American Medical Technologists (AMT), California Certifying Board of Medical Assistants (CMAA). Note: Applicants without a proper certification will not be considered.
High School Diploma or equivalent.
Act in accordance with the highest possible standards of ethics and integrity and comply with work rules, standards, and procedures.
Greets patients, takes vital signs, and prepares patients for exams and special procedures.
Assists clinicians during exams and special procedures.
Fulfills clinician orders for conducting EKG exams, wound cleaning, dressing changes, fitting of a variety of orthopedic appliances, ear lavages, audiogram, nebulizer treatment, peak flow/spirometry.
Responds appropriately in emergency situations as well as with distressed or emergency patients.
Is a team member during the Mass Immunization Clinics at SHS.
Administers oral or injectable medications and/or immunizations in the various clinics as needed.
Performs as a chaperone when needed.
Identifies and completes necessary paperwork accurately and completely.
Obtains medical records and lab and X-ray results when needed.
Restocks supplies, monitors and rotates expiring supplies and medications.
Using universal precautions, cleans up patient emesis, blood, excreta, and body fluids.
Perform point-of-care laboratory testing.
Keeps areas neat, clean and orderly, maintaining a safe environment for patients and co-workers.
Assures accuracy of lab specimens and processing in a timely fashion, walks specimens to lab as needed.
Makes appointments and bills for service rendered via the computer system.
Assists in providing other computer input as needed.
Completes Medical Clearance documents as needed.
May perform prior authorization, referrals, refills, and change appointment times as needed by the demands of the clinic.
Answers phone, relaying accurate messages.
Answers general questions regarding SHS policies and procedures.
Functions as a member of the clinic team assisting with back or front office duties as appropriate, such as, interacting with other units, running errands, etc.

Covered Individuals: A Covered Individual includes anyone designated as Personnel or Students under this Policy who physically access a University Facility or Program in connection with their employment, appointment, or education/training. A person accessing a Healthcare Location as a patient, or an art, athletics, entertainment, or other publicly accessible venue at a Location as a member of the public, is not a Covered Individual.
Knowledge of clinical policies and procedures.
Acquires necessary skills to maintain Autoclave functions and assists as necessary to meet the needs of the clinic.
Knowledge of medical terminology.
Acquires necessary skills to maintain Trophon functions and assists as necessary to meet the needs of the clinic.
Knowledge of electronic medical records and computer skills.
Acquires necessary skills to maintain the laundry functions and assists as necessary to meet the needs of the clinic.
Knowledge of common safety hazards and precautions to establish a safe work environment.
Ability to communicate well with patients, families, co-workers, physicians, advance care providers, other members of the healthcare team, community resources, as well as the campus community.
Ability to organize and prioritize work.
Ability to follow oral and written instructions.
Ability to reason and make sound judgments.
Skilled in identifying problems and recommending solutions.
Skilled in establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with co-workers, management, patients, medical staff, the public, and the campus as a whole.
Skilled in accepting constructive criticism and giving suggestions in a professional manner.
